key_insight: Simulated quantum layers improved VLM accuracy when inserted after the visual projector, while selective replacement reduced trainable parameters with strong accuracy retention.
engineering_relevance: Quantum-layer placement offers an accuracy–parameter trade-off, but fewer parameters do not reliably reduce training time or computation.
method: Use LLaVA-OneVision as the vision-language backbone.
Evaluate classically simulated 4- and 8-qubit basic-ring and strongly entangling circuits.
Compare four insertion and four replacement locations; assess robustness under six attack settings.
evidence_signal: On Visual Spatial Reasoning development data, insertion achieved 80.7% accuracy (+2.28 percentage points over classical full fine-tuning), while final decoder feed-forward replacement achieved 79.22% with 13.07 million fewer trainable parameters.
watch_item: Results rely on classical simulation; generalization, quantum-hardware advantages, and security benefits remain unestablished by the abstract.
paper_title: Can Quantum Layers offer Performance and Security Advantages in Vision-Language Models?
